summary: Concrete light on the northern tip of the Big Island of Hawaii: lit 1897, rebuilt 1933, the tower demolished in December 2009 after cliff erosion; a pole light replaced it.

structures.type: wood-frame tower with enclosed lamp room
structures.status: replaced; a lamp on a thirty-foot mast replaced the tower after 1904 (LighthouseFriends)

structures.type: replacement light set farther back from the cliff edge
structures.status: in place by November 2009 (LighthouseFriends); the Coast Guard had installed a new aid (Demolition News)

access.note: Coast Guard property. Archive: not open to the public. LighthouseFriends (written before the 2009 demolition): grounds open, tower closed; a gate on the approach road may be locked.

visit.note: Tower not open to climb (LighthouseFriends and Archive). The 1933 tower no longer stands.

events.note: Activated by the Hawaiian Government in 1897 (LighthouseFriends).
Lighthouse Board took control of Hawaii's lights; its report found the station dilapidated and with no keeper's residence (LighthouseFriends).
Keeper's dwelling completed 12 January 1914 at a cost of $2,833, roughly 475 feet south of the light (LighthouseFriends).
Commissioner's estimate of $19,000 to improve the station; lens-lantern light to be changed (Commissioner's report, 1915 volume).
Temporary wooden tower; flashing white light of 67,000 candlepower (Bulletin 1933; LighthouseFriends says a pyramidal frame tower with a revolving fourth-order lens).
Fourth-order flash lens with incandescent oil-vapor apparatus on a temporary frame tower (Commissioner's estimate, bound volume; corpus year label 1921, fiscal year not confirmed).
Became a one-keeper station on 16 June 1922 after a thermostat alarm was installed (LighthouseFriends).
Fire in the lantern room, 25 September 1931, apparently from a faulty thermostat; glass broken and lens prisms cracked (LighthouseFriends).
Two generators installed and the light electrified (LighthouseFriends).
Reinforced concrete tower: 72 ft (Bulletin) or 86 ft (LighthouseFriends); cost $17,495 (LighthouseFriends).
Light moved to the new tower on 16 March 1933 (Bulletin).
Earthquake took about six feet off the cliff at once (Demolition News).
Engineering report estimated the tower would likely collapse within two to five years from erosion (LighthouseFriends).
Replacement light (pole, farther inland) in place by November 2009 (LighthouseFriends; Demolition News).
Demolition of the 1933 tower began Friday, 11 December 2009 (Demolition News; LighthouseFriends). Wikipedia gives 12 December (not cited).

notes_for_editor: Story: us-hi-kauhola-point.md (about 1,500 words, five chapters plus Today). Disagreements left open in the story: (a) height of the 1933 tower: 72 ft (Lighthouse Service Bulletin, 1933) vs 86 ft (LighthouseFriends; the record's 26.2 m also equals 86 ft). The HAER report that Wikipedia cites (HAER HI-89) could settle it, but both fetch_text and WebFetch got HTTP 403 for the PDF; not verified. (b) Shoreline distance when built: 85 ft (LighthouseFriends) vs 80 ft (Demolition News). (c) Demolition start: Demolition News (dated 14 Dec 2009) and LighthouseFriends both say Friday, 11 December; Wikipedia (lead, not cited) says 12 December. The story uses 11 December. (d) Demolition duration: LighthouseFriends three days; Demolition News three to five days. (e) Access: Archive 'not open to the public' vs LighthouseFriends 'grounds open, tower closed' (written before demolition). Coast Guard property. (f) 1904-1917 light: LighthouseFriends says a lamp on a thirty-foot mast replaced the wooden tower after 1904; the 1933 Bulletin says a fixed white light on a 30-foot mast ran up to 1917. Consistent enough; the story says 'at some point after 1904'. Record fixes: status and structure (see corrections). The record's characteristic (Fl W 15s), focal height (32.9 m) and range (10 nm) are not supported by any source read here; the Wikipedia infobox for the 2009 light gives a stainless steel pole, solar power and white flashing once every 15 seconds, but Wikipedia is lead-only and was not cited. Bulletin 1933 page 10 OCR garbles the liner's name; the story says 'a liner's second officer' and quotes only the distance wording. Bulletin 1933 page 14 OCR has stray tokens (for example 'KAWAU') before the paragraph; the quoted words are clean. Keepers: all 18 lines from the Archive roster (cite 1 with person slugs). LighthouseFriends' assistant-keeper list was truncated in our read, so no extra stints were added. Chronicling America search results for Kauhola in Hawaii papers were mostly noise; one page (Hawaiian Gazette, 18 October 1910, p. 5) was read; its OCR is rough. The 1897 construction is not covered by any newspaper page checked here. Not used: Wikipedia except as a lead; the Graham's Island blog (2017) describes a metal-pole light, unverified. Access and safety: the approach crosses Coast Guard property; the story says a closed gate is not to be passed. Photos: none new (the record's Commons images were not reviewed). Verification pass corrections: the Hawaiian Gazette (18 Oct 1910, p. 5) gives the right of way to the Mahukona land ('the former') and says no such provision was made for Kauhola, so the story and evidence no longer tie the right of way to Kauhola; the Commissioner's 1921-labelled estimate (scan 693) is cited without a fiscal year because the text does not fix one; 'steps have been taken to change' is now quoted in place of 'would be changed'; LighthouseFriends' title for R.R. Tinkham is superintendent of the lighthouse of Hawaii, not a district superintendent; 'Kohala' is cited to the Bulletin. Hawaii County is the brief's local_unit.
